title: The First Detection of the 232 GHz Vibrationally Excited H<SUB>2</SUB>O Maser in Orion KL with ALMA
question: Is there a vibrationally excited H2O maser at 232.68670 GHz in Orion KL, blended with HCOOCH3, and where is it located?

data.bands: Band 6 (215-245 GHz) SV spectral line survey; Cycle 0 band 6 continuum at 240-244 and 256-260 GHz
data.angular_resolution: SV natural-weighted beam 1.7"x1.4", PA 171 deg; Cycle 0 uniform-weighted 0.74"x0.56", PA 101 deg

what.value: 22 GHz H2O shell maser spectrum compared with the 232 GHz feature

evidence.quote: appears to be analogous to the 22 GHz shell masers (cite: gaume1998)

what.value: Line frequencies from Splatalogue (JPL, CDMS, Lovas/NIST)

evidence.quote: Splatalogue[^1], which is a compilation of the JPL, CDMS, and Lovas/NIST catalogs (cite: pickett1998; muller2005; lovas2004)

recipe.goal: Image the blended and pure HCOOCH3 features
recipe.method: Synthesis imaging of calibrated SV data around 232.68 and 232.74 GHz

recipe.goal: Isolate H2O emission by map subtraction
recipe.method: Subtract pure HCOOCH3 map from blended map; residual concentrated at Source I
assumptions: Pure line has similar frequency, lower-state energy and expected intensity to the blended HCOOCH3 line

recipe.method: Channel maps and spectra at selected positions; two-component Gaussian fit to Source I spectrum
Peak 0.43 Jy in 2x2 arcsec aperture gives 2.4 K; diluted to 0.01 K in a 30 arcsec single-dish beam
assumptions: Emitting region as compact as the aperture

evidence.quote: 0.28$\pm$0.02 Jy and 0.43$\pm$0.02 Jy at the velocity of $-$2.1$\pm$0.6 km s$^{-1}$ and 13.3$\pm$0.4 km s$^{-1}$
0.28$\pm$0.02 Jy and 0.43$\pm$0.02 Jy at the velocity of $-$2.1$\pm$0.6 km s$^{-1}$ and 13.3$\pm$0.4 km s$^{-1}$
at the velocity of $-$2.1$\pm$0.6 km s$^{-1}$ and 13.3$\pm$0.4 km s$^{-1}$
It corresponds to the brightness temperature of 2.4 K.
